title: Probation Prep Pack
description: The composite playbook for a PO's final 21 days of probation. Four sub-artefacts. The PO's evidence base is different from BA/PM/SM — the PO is being assessed on judgement under pressure and on the discipline of saying no. The signature is the un-roadmap: the things the PO decided against, with reasoning. The worked conversation example is annotated turn by turn.

# Probation Prep Pack — Product Owner
_Four sub-artefacts. Self-assessment, pre-review 1:1 agenda, evidence portfolio (with un-roadmap), worked conversation. Rehearse last._

## Sub-artefact 1: Self-Assessment

One page. Three columns.

| Decided | Learned | Want next |
|---------|---------|-----------|
_'Decided' instead of 'delivered'. The PO's job is judgement, not output. Three to five items in each column, including at least two decisions where the answer was 'no'._

## Sub-artefact 2: Pre-Review 1:1 Agenda

Thirty minutes, booked a week before the formal review. Framing:

> 'I want to walk into our review well-prepared. Specifically, I want to understand which of my decisions this quarter you'd defend with me and which you'd have made differently.'

The PO-specific reframe is asking your manager to be candid about decisions she might disagree with — before the formal review puts you both on the spot.

### Agenda

1. **My read of the quarter's decisions** (3 minutes). One paragraph.
2. **The hardest no I held, and the no I'm least confident I should have held** (5 minutes).
3. **Your read — which decisions you'd defend, which you'd revisit** (15 minutes). Listen.
4. **What 'a strong PO in this role' looks like in a year** (5 minutes).
5. **What you'd like me to surface in the formal review** (2 minutes).

## Sub-artefact 3: Evidence Portfolio (with Un-Roadmap)

_Two parts. The shipped work, and crucially the un-roadmap — the things you decided against and why._

### Shipped (3-5 items, with the user outcome each one served)

| Item | Date | User outcome it served | What you decided was important |
|------|------|------------------------|--------------------------------|
|      |      |                        |                                |

### Un-roadmap (3-5 items, with the reasoning)

| Item | Decided | Why no | Trade-off accepted |
|------|---------|--------|--------------------|
|      |         |        |                    |

_The un-roadmap is the PO-signature artefact. Most candidates skip it. Don't._

## Sub-artefact 4: The Conversation Playbook

_See the annotated worked example below._

worked_examples.content_md:
# The Product Owner Probation Review — Worked Example

_Setting: Bilqis Hassan (VP Product Strategy, hiring manager) and the PO. Day 88. Thirty minutes. The team likes the PO; Folake is enthusiastic in writing; Daniel has complained twice. The June-launch conversation in week 6 is in the file._

---

**Bilqis:** Tell me about a decision you made this quarter that you'd defend even if it cost us a stakeholder.

_[**PO's silent thought:** This is the opener. She isn't asking about wins; she's asking about judgement under cost. The partner-referral 'no' is the obvious answer. Open with it.]_

**PO:** The partner referral codes no, in week 7. Daniel raised it three times by then; the third time was in the stakeholder forum in front of Tobi. I held the no. Daniel escalated once after that, and I think a second time though I didn't see that one directly.

_[**Annotation:** Names the specific decision in one sentence. Doesn't hide the consequence (escalations). Doesn't perform regret. Opens factually.]_

**Bilqis:** Walk me through the reasoning.

**PO:** The data team's model assumed 12% adoption; the realistic base case is closer to 5%, which makes the expected value about £80k not £400k. Six weeks of build plus a compliance review. The slot would have displaced the bulk-import work, which has a tighter probability distribution and a stronger fit with the portal investment we'd already made. I wrote it up as a memo — sent to Daniel and Tobi. The memo's in the file.

_[**Annotation:** Specific numbers. Names the trade-off accepted (the displacement). References the written artefact. Tells Bilqis the work was real and documented, without being defensive.]_

**Bilqis:** And if I told you Tobi thought you were wrong?

_[**PO's silent thought:** This is the test. She's asking whether I cave under hierarchical pressure or whether I hold the no. The answer is to neither cave nor harden — defend the reasoning, accept that someone senior to me disagrees.]_

**PO:** I'd want to know which assumption Tobi disagrees with — the adoption rate, the displacement choice, or the strategic-fit framing. If it's the adoption rate, that's the kind of disagreement that's resolvable with better data; I'd want to see his number. If it's the strategic-fit framing, that's a judgement disagreement and I'd want to hear his reasoning. But I'd defend the decision against the original proposal, yes.

_[**Annotation:** Doesn't capitulate ('I'd reconsider'). Doesn't harden ('I'm right'). Names the structural question — which part of the reasoning is contested. This is the answer that shows Bilqis the PO can hold a no without breaking a relationship.]_

**Bilqis:** OK. What about the date-pressure conversation in week 6 — the bulk-import + reports + billing one.

_[**PO's silent thought:** She's bringing up the conversation where I pushed back on her, in front of her peers. She's testing whether I remember it the same way she does.]_

**PO:** I offered to commit to one of the three by mid-June and to come back with sized estimates on the other two by the following Friday. I think the offer was the right shape. I think I could have offered it earlier in the meeting — there was about a 90-second window where I was clearly working out my answer in real time, and the room saw me think.

_[**Annotation:** Names what they handled well AND the thing they'd do differently. Bilqis can see this PO has rehearsed the moment in their head and is honest about the gap. Doesn't apologise; just names.]_

**Bilqis:** Yes. I noticed. I appreciated the offer; I noticed the 90 seconds.

_[**PO's silent thought:** She saw it. She wasn't going to bring it up unless I did. Glad I did.]_

**Bilqis:** What's the no you're least confident about?

**PO:** The historical-data migration. I declined that at programme charter; Folake didn't push back at the time, but two of the top-12 (Forrest Bank specifically) have asked about it in QBRs since. The reasoning at the time was capacity — it would have been a 4-week separate workstream. I'd still make the same call now, but I'd have had a written conversation with Folake about it at the time so she had the rationale to take to her customers. I didn't do that.

_[**Annotation:** Names a real uncertainty without disclaiming the decision. Specific. Self-aware. The 'I'd still make the same call' line is important — it stops this becoming a regret narrative.]_

**Bilqis:** Right. That's the answer I was looking for. 

_[**Annotation:** Bilqis is signalling. The PO has demonstrated the two things being assessed: hold a no, articulate a doubt without retreating. This is the moment Bilqis decides whether the PO can take harder assignments.]_

**Bilqis:** There's a product area I'm thinking about restructuring in Q4 — partner integrations. It's adjacent to your portal work. If we did, I'd want a PO who can say no to Sales weekly without it becoming a thing. Is that something you'd want?

**PO:** I'd want it. I'd want to spend two weeks in the area before the formal restructure — partly to learn the partner-integrations work, partly because the Sales relationships in that area are different from the Folake/Yetunde axis I've been working in this quarter. The Sales push will be weekly, you're right; I haven't been tested on weekly push from one specific partner-management surface.

_[**Annotation:** Accepts the offer. Names specifically what they'd want to learn first. Acknowledges the gap honestly — they haven't yet been tested on a single sales surface pushing weekly. This is the answer that distinguishes confirmed-and-trusted-with-harder-work from just confirmed.]_

**Bilqis:** Let me see what I can land.

---

_The PO walked out without an explicit confirmed yes but with two pieces of information. Bilqis was thinking about their next role before the conversation. 'That's the answer I was looking for' was the closest thing to a yes the meeting was going to produce._

annotations.note: Self-assessment uses 'Decided' instead of 'Delivered'. This is the PO-specific structural difference. The PO's job is judgement; the language of the assessment should match. Include at least two decisions where the answer was 'no'.

The pre-review 1:1 question — 'which of my decisions you'd defend with me and which you'd have made differently' — is the PO-specific reframe. Most candidates ask for feedback; the PO asks the manager to be candid about decisions she might disagree with. The difference matters.

The un-roadmap is the PO-signature artefact. Most candidates present a shipping log; the PO presents both the shipping log AND the un-roadmap. Without the un-roadmap, the evidence portfolio is incomplete and Bilqis-class reviewers will notice.

The annotated conversation shows the structural moves: open with the hardest decision, accept consequences without performing regret, name the structural question when challenged, name your own uncertainty without disclaiming the decision. Read twice.

common_mistakes: Self-assessment listing only shipped features. The PO's job is judgement; demonstrating judgement requires showing the decisions, including the no's. List both.
Pre-review 1:1 framed as 'what can I improve'. Wrong question. The right question is 'which of my decisions would you defend and which would you revisit'. Forces a sharper conversation.
Un-roadmap omitted from evidence portfolio. The most common PO-probation-pack failure. Without it, the review reads as 'PO who ships things' rather than 'PO who makes calls'.
Worked-conversation playbook skimmed once. Read it twice. The second read teaches the structural moves.
Treating the review as a presentation of the pack. The pack is so the conversation can happen; presenting it page by page wastes the conversation.
Answering the 'no you're least confident about' question with 'none, I'd defend all of them'. Loses credibility instantly. There is always at least one real doubt; name it.
variant_patterns: Extended-probation variant: the conversation playbook reshapes around 'what specifically would land as continued in the next 30 days?' — pulling specific behavioural changes from the reviewer.

First-PO-in-the-team variant (no previous PO to compare against): the evidence portfolio shifts to include 'what we introduced and the team kept' (refinement discipline, AC patterns, prioritisation conversations). Probation will partly assess whether the role's existence is justified.
Non-standard probation length variant: structure unchanged. Probation Mode activates 21 days before the actual review date, whatever its length.
